(1) The distinction between necessary and dynamic IC's is important for KB modeling, (2) The distinction is best captured in a framework that includes a dynamic component (dynamic logic), and (3) The framework should be extended to include a deontic component to capture the distinction between deontic and non-deontic constraints

the difference between dynamic, deontic, and static IC's is significant, that dynamic and deontics IC's can be specified using the same framework, that the difference between static and dynamic IC's is significant for the KB designer, and that the difference between deontic and non-deontic IC's can be significant as well.

(1) there are two types of integrity constraints: deontic (UoD constraints) and necessary (implementation constraints); (2) both types of constraints are needed in KB modeling; and (3) a dynamic deontic logic is a suitable formalism for the specification of both types of constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling of knowledge bases and the specification of integrity constraints.
the modeling of dynamic and deontics IC's in KB's.
the specification of dynamic and deontically constrained KB's, and with the specification of the dynamic aspects of such KB's.

the distinction between deontic and dynamic constraints is relevant for KB's, and that it imposes an additional modeling discipline on the designer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the first framework that allows for a uniform treatment of static, dynamic and dynamic deontic constraints in a KB.
the deontic logic framework can be used as a general framework for specifying dynamic constraints, and in particular for specifying deontic integrity constraints.
we have provided the KB designer with the tools for a more sophisticated modeling of KB's.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modeling discipline of a KB designer should be more complicated than hitherto assumed, and that the distinction between deontic and dynamic constraints should be made explicit.
the specification of deontics and dynamics in a single framework provides the means of expressing a wide range of constraints, and that this framework can be used for the specification of KB's.
the KB designer should be aware of the difference between the two types of IC's, and that the KB designer's task is more complex than previously thought.
